overall_status_rationale: Every FR is implemented and all 21 test cases pass, with zero regressions in the 86 pre-existing ones. The roll-up is 'partial' rather than 'compliant' because FR-085 ships with one DECLARED piece of debt: the gateway probe is identified by its label rather than structurally, so an operator who renames that target would get a less precise verdict ('Unstable' instead of 'Offline') on a broken LAN. That is contained and graceful, but it is the same class of weakness that caused BG-074, so it is named rather than hidden.
deployment_target: Raspberry Pi (ARM64) — native binary + systemd. Unchanged.

binaries: ultron-ap only — ultron-helper is NOT touched; no privilege change, no new host action
deployment_artifacts.schema_migration: NONE. This feature touches no database. Rollback is trivially safe: the previous binary renders the previous tile from the same DashboardData.
deployment_artifacts.static_assets: make css added exactly one class (space-y-0.5) and removed none; the rebuilt app.css is committed. Skipping this would have shipped the disclosure's row spacing unstyled — the same trap the hardware section nearly fell into.

environment_variables.name: ULTRON_NET_TARGETS
environment_variables.notes: The verdict consumes these probes. IMPORTANT: renaming the gateway target away from the label 'gateway' degrades the verdict (see technical debt) — a broken LAN would read 'Unstable' rather than 'Offline'.

requirement_compliance.title: Network tile shows a link-state verdict as its headline
requirement_compliance.evidence: 6 test cases, all passing. TC-NT-085h (all probes healthy => 'Stable' + 'WAN up · 0% loss'), TC-NT-085e (8.8.8.8 at 15% loss => 'Unstable', and the reason NAMES the failing target), TC-NT-085f (WAN monitor down => 'Offline'), TC-NT-085Bf (gateway timing out => 'Offline', not merely unstable — a broken LAN is a different problem), TC-NT-085Be (no probes => 'unknown'; the tile never claims a state it cannot know and falls back to throughput), TC-NT-085Bh (a SINGLE dropped ping = 5% loss must NOT flip the tile — a >0% rule would cry wolf on a healthy home link). Thresholds are the existing latencyCrit* constants, so the tile can never disagree with the sparklines below it. DECLARED DEBT: the gateway is identified by label, not structurally.

requirement_compliance.title: Throughput subtitle; per-interface detail one click away
requirement_compliance.evidence: 6 test cases, all passing. TC-NT-086h (the subtitle names eth0 with both rates; idle interfaces appear only inside the disclosure), TC-NT-086e (the <details> carries no 'open' attribute — closed by default), TC-NT-089h (expanded, every non-virtual interface is listed), TC-NT-086f (the busiest interface is max(sent+recv), NEVER a sum: tailscale0 tunnels over eth0, and summing would report 110 KB/s for 60 KB/s of real traffic — the test asserts no summed total appears anywhere), TC-NT-089f (docker0/br-*/veth*/lo never reappear — the BG-072 filter holds), TC-NT-090f (stripping the disclosure from the HTML leaves no interface row behind). Browser-verified: 124px collapsed vs 432px expanded.

requirement_compliance.title: The tile absorbs the loose WAN chip
requirement_compliance.evidence: 3 test cases, all passing. TC-NT-087h (the tile carries 'WAN up' and the standalone chip markup is gone from the page), TC-NT-087f (WAN down => the tile reads 'Offline' with metric-critical, and there is still no second WAN element — one source of truth), TC-NT-087e (a nil WAN snapshot claims nothing and does not crash the template). Browser-verified: the page no longer contains the orphan chip.

requirement_compliance.title: Regression — the other tiles and the SSE refresh are untouched
requirement_compliance.evidence: TC-NT-088h (CPU 22.2%, Memory 45.7%, Disk 8.2% and Temp 51°C all still render with their thresholds), TC-NT-088f (a nil probe entry does not panic — a panic here would kill the dashboard for every connected SSE client), TC-NT-085Be (an empty probe list still renders the partial). TC-NT-E2E-002h renders through the SSE FuncMap specifically, because templates.go carries TWO FuncMaps and registering the new funcs in only one fails silently in the other path. The full 86-case suite passes unchanged.

requirement_compliance.title: Regression — the BG-072 filter and BG-073 history fix survive
requirement_compliance.evidence: TC-NT-089f (no virtual interface appears, expanded or not), TC-NT-089h (the real ones do), TC-NT-088e (a host whose only interface is docker0 still sees its traffic — the filter falls back rather than emptying the tile). The BG-073 fix (sparkline history read by label) is untouched by this feature and its test still passes.

requirement_compliance.title: Compactness and touch target
requirement_compliance.evidence: TC-NT-090h (the <summary> carries the min-h-[44px] marker the project enforces everywhere), TC-NT-086e (closed by default), TC-NT-090f (no row leaks outside the disclosure). Measured in Chrome: the tile's content height is 124px collapsed — comparable to its neighbours — versus 432px expanded.

test_evidence.result: 21/21 passing (19 unit + integration, 2 e2e) — verified by aitri feature verify-complete
test_evidence.full_suite: go vet ./... clean; go test ./... green — the 86 pre-existing test cases pass unchanged
test_evidence.browser: Chrome against the running app: details.open == false on load, 124px collapsed / 432px expanded, no orphan WAN chip, and the tile renders through both the page path and the SSE path.

non_functional_compliance.performance: One pass over <=4 probe snapshots and <=5 filtered interfaces per rendered partial — the same tick that already renders CPU/RAM/Disk/Temp. No new query, no new goroutine, no new I/O, no database access. On a Pi this is microseconds.
non_functional_compliance.security: No new route, handler, parameter, privileged call or database access. Interface names (from the kernel) and probe labels (from operator config) render through html/template, which escapes them. The verdict word is a closed set chosen by the server, never client input. The whole page is already behind requireAuth.
non_functional_compliance.ci_cd: The existing GitHub Actions workflow covers it: the new tests are pure-function and rendered-HTML tests — no browser, no sleeps, no flake.

technical_debt_inherited.substitution: The gateway probe is identified by matching the label 'gateway'. Renaming that target via ULTRON_NET_TARGETS leaves the verdict with no gateway clause, so a broken LAN would read 'Unstable' instead of 'Offline'.
technical_debt_inherited.reason: gatewayprobe.Snapshot does not carry the probe's configured Host, so the gateway cannot be identified structurally from the snapshot. This is the same class of weakness that produced BG-074 (a rule keyed on a label no target carried) — named here rather than hidden.
technical_debt_inherited.remediation: Carry the configured Host (or an IsGateway flag) into gatewayprobe.Snapshot and identify the gateway structurally. It belongs in gatewayprobe, not the tile. Until then the degradation is graceful: the tile still warns, with a less precise word.

owner_feedback_closed: 'Es confuso para un elemento principal' — the tile now leads with one word (Stable/Unstable/Offline) like every other tile in the row, instead of three rows of byte counters.
'O cambiarlo por un indicador general, o un estable/no-estable' — delivered, reusing the probes and thresholds the panel already had rather than inventing new ones.
'Casi nunca lo miro' (the throughput) — it is now the subtitle, and the per-interface breakdown is one click away instead of occupying the tile.
